options: The sum of absolute distances from each point to its centroid
The sum of squared distances from each point to its assigned centroid (WCSS)
The maximum distance between any two points in the same cluster
The between-cluster sum of squares
questions.explanation: k-means minimises the Within-Cluster Sum of Squares (WCSS) = Σₖ Σᵢ∈Cₖ ||xᵢ − μₖ||². Using squared distances means the optimal centroid is the arithmetic mean of the cluster's points, making the update step a simple average.

questions.text: Why do we set nstart = 25 when calling kmeans() in R?
options: To run 25 clustering iterations before convergence
To try 25 different random initialisations and keep the solution with the lowest WCSS
To set the maximum number of clusters to 25
To ensure the algorithm runs for at least 25 seconds
questions.explanation: Lloyd's algorithm converges to a local minimum that depends on the initial centroid positions. Running nstart = 25 repetitions with different random starts increases the probability of finding the global (best) local minimum. The run with the lowest WCSS is returned.

questions.text: In the elbow method, WCSS always decreases as k increases. What does the 'elbow' represent?
options: The k value with the lowest WCSS
The k value beyond which adding more clusters gives diminishing returns in WCSS reduction
The k value that maximises the silhouette score
The point where WCSS stops decreasing
questions.explanation: WCSS always decreases as k increases (at k = n, WCSS = 0). The elbow is the inflection point where the rate of decrease sharply slows — adding more clusters beyond this point gives little additional compactness but increases model complexity.

questions.text: A silhouette score of −0.3 for a data point means:
options: The point is well-clustered and far from other clusters
The point is on the boundary between two clusters
The point is closer to another cluster than to its own cluster — it may be misclassified
The clustering algorithm did not converge for this point
questions.explanation: Silhouette score s(i) = (b(i) − a(i)) / max(a(i), b(i)). When s(i) < 0, it means b(i) < a(i): the point's average distance to its own cluster is greater than its average distance to the nearest other cluster. This indicates the point is likely in the wrong cluster.

questions.text: k-means clustering requires you to scale your features before fitting, because the algorithm is distance-based.
questions.explanation: k-means uses Euclidean distance. If one feature (e.g., income in thousands) has a much larger scale than another (e.g., age in years), income will dominate the distance calculation and effectively determine cluster membership. Z-score standardisation puts all features on equal footing.

questions.text: You cluster 50,000 policyholders into 4 groups. Cluster 3 has average age = 67, average chronic conditions = 3.1, and high claim amounts. What label best describes this cluster for business use?
options: Young healthy low-risk policyholders
Middle-income moderate-risk policyholders
Elderly high-utilisation policyholders — likely to have high claims
High-income premium plan seekers
questions.explanation: Old age, high chronic conditions, and high claims are strongly associated with heavy healthcare utilisation. This cluster is best labelled as elderly high-utilisation — a segment that warrants different pricing, care management, and retention strategies.
